title: Given an array and two values K1 and K2, find the sum of all elements that are strictly greater than the K1-th smallest and strictly smaller than the K2-th smallest. Explain how two heaps, or finding the two order statistics, let you sum the band in between.
shortTitle: Sum of Elements Between K1 and K2 Smallest (Sum Strictly Between Two Order Statistics)

s1_definition.profdef: Sum of Elements Between K1 and K2 Smallest is a Top K Elements problem. The elements strictly between the K1-th and K2-th smallest are exactly the ones whose rank is from K1 plus one up to K2 minus one. Using a max-heap of size K2, we can pop the K2-th through just-after-K1-th smallest, summing the ones we want, so we obtain the band without fully sorting.
s1_definition.analogy: At the National Bank of India, we rank account balances and want the total of the balances that sit strictly between the K1-th smallest and the K2-th smallest, excluding both endpoints, for a mid-tier analysis. We use a heap to peel off balances by rank and add up only those falling in the middle band.
s1_definition.oneliner: The target elements have ranks K1 plus one through K2 minus one; use a size-K2 max-heap to peel them off and sum them.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Sum of Elements Between K1 and K2 Smallest is a Top K Elements problem. The elements strictly between the K1-th and K2-th smallest are exactly the ones whose rank is from K1 plus one up to K2 minus one. Using a max-heap of size K2, we can pop the K2-th through just-after-K1-th smallest, summing the ones we want, so we obtain the band without fully sorting.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** At the National Bank of India, we rank account balances and want the total of the balances that sit strictly between the K1-th smallest and the K2-th smallest, excluding both endpoints, for a mid-tier analysis. We use a heap to peel off balances by rank and add up only those falling in the middle band.

**One line to remember:** The target elements have ranks K1 plus one through K2 minus one; use a size-K2 max-heap to peel them off and sum them.

sections.s2_technical:
One clean method uses a max-heap of size K2. We push numbers, keeping only the K2 smallest, so after processing the heap holds the K2 smallest numbers with the largest, the K2-th smallest, at the root. We then pop the root once to discard the K2-th smallest itself, since the band is strictly below it, and then pop and sum the next elements until only K1 remain in the heap, which correspond to ranks one through K1 that we must exclude. For example, after building the size-K2 max-heap, `maxHeap.poll(); while (maxHeap.size() > k1) sum += maxHeap.poll();`.

The remaining K1 elements in the heap are the K1 smallest, which are excluded, and the one we popped first was the K2-th smallest, also excluded, so what we summed is exactly ranks K1 plus one through K2 minus one. Building the heap is O(n log K2) and the final pops are O(K2 log K2).

A senior nuance is that an even simpler approach, when a full sort is acceptable, sorts once and sums the slice from index K1 to K2 minus two, which is O(n log n); the heap method is preferable when K2 is much smaller than n. Being careful with the strict exclusions at both ends, discarding the K2-th smallest and leaving the K1 smallest, is the correctness crux. Complexity is O(n log K2) time and O(K2) space.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — The National Bank of India analyses account balances and needs the total of the balances ranked strictly between the K1-th smallest and the K2-th smallest, excluding both endpoints, for a mid-tier segment study. This is exactly how Sum Between K1 and K2 Smallest works.

Problem 2 — Fully sorting all balances is more than needed when K2 is small. This is why we keep a size-K2 max-heap of the K2 smallest balances and peel off exactly the middle band to sum.

The code defines a `BalanceBandService` exposing `sumBetween(balances, k1, k2)` returning the band sum. A `Demo` sums the mid-tier balances and logs the total.

sections.s5_journey:
Input: balances 1000, 3000, 12000, 5000, 15000, 7000 with K1 equal to 2 and K2 equal to 5. Sorted, these are 1000, 3000, 5000, 7000, 12000, 15000.

Step 1: Build a size-five max-heap keeping the five smallest balances 1000, 3000, 5000, 7000, 12000; the root is 12000, the fifth smallest.

Step 2: Discard the root 12000, the K2-th smallest, which is excluded from the band.

Step 3: Now pop while more than K1 equal to two remain. Pop 7000 and add it; pop 5000 and add it. The heap now holds 1000 and 3000, exactly K1 equal to two elements, so we stop.

Step 4: The summed band is 7000 plus 5000 equals 12000, the balances strictly between the second and fifth smallest.

```

INFO: Sum between 2th and 5th smallest = 12000
INFO: Mid-tier balance sum: 12000
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  balances → size-K2(=5) max-heap keeps 5 smallest
    │ root = 5th smallest = 12000
    ▼
  poll root (discard 12000, upper endpoint excluded)
    │ pop while size > K1(=2): +7000, +5000
    │ remaining {1000,3000} = K1 smallest (excluded)
    ▼
  band sum = 12000
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
Sum of Elements Between K1 and K2 Smallest asks for the total of the elements whose rank falls strictly between the K1-th smallest and the K2-th smallest, excluding both endpoints, so the target ranks are K1 plus one through K2 minus one. I solve it with a single size-K2 max-heap. I push every number but keep the heap trimmed to K2, so it ends holding exactly the K2 smallest numbers with the K2-th smallest sitting at the root.

Then I peel off the band precisely. I first pop the root once to discard the K2-th smallest, because the upper endpoint is excluded. After that I keep popping and summing until only K1 elements remain in the heap; those remaining K1 are the K1 smallest, which are also excluded. Everything I summed in between is exactly ranks K1 plus one through K2 minus one, so the two strict exclusions are handled by one discard at the top and by stopping when K1 elements are left at the bottom.

At the National Bank of India I used this for a mid-tier segment study that needed the total of account balances ranked strictly between two order statistics, without the cost of fully sorting every balance when the band was small. I kept a size-K2 max-heap of the smallest balances and peeled off the middle band. Explaining the rank arithmetic, the two strict exclusions, and why the max-heap gives n log K2 rather than n log n is what shows an interviewer I handle order statistics carefully.
